headline: Sensex and Nifty end lower as banking and pharma stocks drag, while IT stocks rally

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Banking, pharma, and auto stocks witnessed significant selling pressure
Volatility in trade led to Sensex dropping over 200 points from previous levels
Margin contractions in corporate earnings impacted investor sentiment
Pharma and financial sectors struggled throughout the trading session
whatHappening: Cabinet approved Fairfax’s ₹52,878-crore bid for IDBI Bank, the largest FDI in India’s financial sector
IT stocks including Infosys and TCS rallied to cushion the broader market fall
Tata Technologies reported a 5% decline in Q2 net profit due to contracting margins
SEBI called a SMAC meeting to review public feedback on Consolidated Account Statements
summary: The Indian stock market ended lower on October 14, with the Nifty 50 closing below 22,650 amid volatile trading. While the IT sector saw gains led by Infosys and TCS, heavy selling in banking, pharma, and auto stocks weighed on the indices. A significant development was the government's approval of the ₹52,878-crore Fairfax bid for IDBI Bank.
